content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I haven't come across a related topic, so I'll explain my situation. My projects are mostly managed via web browser, and I want to load any image onto the [product_name] or [product_name] operator panel. For example, displaying a logo, a STOP sign, or directional arrows for rotation. The screen size makes text harder to read, and the display is often cluttered. Even if I configure a text screen with the word "STOP" in red, the message isn't easily noticeable at a glance. I've tried using symbols like ^, >, <, and solid blocks to create large text messages such as "DROP" and "LIFT" on the screen. However, these do not render properly on the web interface—alignment is inconsistent. It does appear correctly on the actual [product_name] itself. Any advice?
No, it isn't possible to show pictures (animated or static) on the [product_name] display or its operator panel.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter limitations in enhancing visual elements on [product_name] screens and operator panels, particularly with showing images or icons for easier recognition. Efforts to improve text size and formatting for clarity don't carry over to web browser access, leading to a less effective user experience when monitoring remotely. The main insight is a gap between user expectations for visualization and the technical constraints of the device displays.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to upload and display images on [product_name] and operator panels for more graphical and user-friendly interfaces, especially when viewed through a web browser. They also expect text formatting and alignment to be consistent between the physical devices and remote web access.
